title: Soundscape and natural landscape as a design construct for improving psycho-physiological health in cities: a semi-systematic literature review

findings.antecedent: Exposure to natural sound and visual environments
findings.quote: exposure to natural sound and visual environments was associated with slower heart rates

findings.antecedent: Exposure to natural sound and visual environments
key_citations: Ochiai, Ikei, Song, Kobayashi, Takamatsu, et al. 2015
Ochiai, Ikei, Song, Kobayashi, Miura, et al. 2015
findings.quote: greater parasympathetic nerve activation.
The presentation of complex audio-visual environments demonstrated that visual signals stimulate the brain area that activates physio-psychological relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Combined effect of natural landscape and soundscape
findings.quote: Overall, the combined effect of natural landscape and soundscape may improve psychophysiological health and should be considered when considering future planning and management of urban environments.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to natural settings (green space, bird songs, natural sounds, visible vegetation)
findings.quote: Studies have shown that exposure to a natural settings, especially green space, which includes bird songs and calls (Ratcliffe et al. 2013, Ratcliffe 2021), and the inclusion of natural sounds and visible vegetation, can have a positive impact on human health and well-being in urban public spaces

findings.antecedent: Absence of green settings (with human-generated sounds and visually complex stimuli)
findings.quote: The absence of green settings, which are often connected with a variety of human-generated sounds and visually complex stimuli, can have a negative impact on mood states

findings.consequent: Physiological and psychological relaxation (increased alpha waves, decreased beta waves, improved mood status)
findings.quote: Forest external space performed best in the area of physiological and psychological relaxation (increased alpha waves, decreased beta waves and improved mood status), followed by forest path space, and finally forest interior space.

findings.direction: significantly lower levels than unmanaged forest
findings.quote: After viewing the unmanaged forest and managed forest, blood pressure, and saliva cortisol both dropped dramatically, with the managed forest having significantly lower levels than the unmanaged forest.

findings.antecedent: Forest therapy program (forest scenery, auditory, olfactory, tactile)
findings.consequent: Anxiety and mood states (confusion, exhaustion, anger-hostility, tension)
findings.quote: A visit to the forest dramatically decreased anxiety and mood states (i.e. confusion, exhaustion, anger-hostility, and tension).
A substantial decrease in systolic blood pressure response was observed after the forest therapy program.
Viewing green sceneries was associated with lower blood pressure, lower heart rate, and higher indices of heart rate variability compared to viewing the city centre.

findings.consequent: Neuronal activity in brain focus area
findings.quote: Water increased neuronal activity in the brain focus area compared with urban and mountain landscapes.

findings.consequent: Pulse rate, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure
findings.quote: Forest bathing program reduced pulse rate, systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure dramatically.

findings.consequent: Affective benefits (reduced anxiety, rumination, neural activity in mental illness risk region)
findings.quote: When compared to walks through a urban environments, nature walks resulted in affective benefits such as reduced anxiety, rumination, and neural activity in a brain region linked to mental illness risk.

findings.consequent: Stress (muscle tension, pulse rate, self-reported stress)
findings.quote: Nature sounds of less than 7 min lowered stress (muscle tension, pulse rate, and self-reported stress) in the experimental group, no significant differences were revealed in the control/classical music groups.
Pleasant soundscapes facilitated faster recovery from stress compared to unpleasant soundscapes.
Experience of unpleasant soundscapes at rest was associated with higher skin conductance level and lower heart rate compared to pleasant soundscapes.

findings.antecedent: Sounds of nature (twittering birds, babbling brook) in virtual green environment
findings.quote: The addition of sounds of nature to a virtual green environment relieved people from stress.
Nature sounds of fountains and tweeting birds lessened psychological stress and facilitated the physiological recovery of the sympathetic nervous system

findings.antecedent: Natural sounds (e.g., babies crying, birds twitter)
findings.consequent: Startle reflexes, corrugator electromyography activity, heart rate deceleration
findings.quote: Natural sounds induced larger startle reflexes elicited higher corrugator electromyography activity, and larger heart rate deceleration compared with perception to natural sounds

findings.antecedent: Natural visual context with auditory stimuli
findings.quote: auditory pleasantness was higher when accompanied by a natural visual context
visual pleasantness was higher when accompanied by natural sounds.
natural sounds were associated with lower heart rate and reduced muscle activity in the eyebrow region
natural images were linked to slower gaze behavior.
Pupil area exhibited sensitivity to both auditory and visual stimuli, constricting in response to natural stimuli

findings.antecedent: Presence of nature in urban environments (audiovisual interactions)
findings.quote: the presence of nature in urban environments improved wellbeing and reduced arousal levels.

findings.antecedent: Sound in combination with static images
findings.quote: Sound in combination with static images resulted in more physiological relaxation.
Static images elicited more physiological relaxation than dynamic videos.

the rural setting led to better psycho-physiological recovery compared to the urban setting in both virtual reality and screen conditions. Particularly, the rural setting with water features evoked the greatest recovery.
the inclusion of water sounds to an urban environment can result in informational or energetic masking of road traffic noise.

findings.consequent: Cacophonies of sound sources (traffic noise, sound reflection)
findings.quote: Vegetation (e.g. trees, green areas, and other types of plants) reduced cacophonies of sound sources, such as annoyance from traffic noise, sound reflection from hard surfaces of roads and buildings/atriums or courtyards
having a view of vegetation reduces the discomfort caused by road noise by 8% when compared to having no view of vegetation at all

Bird sounds are naturally perceived as restorative and have been shown to be beneficial for positive feelings and emotions (Nilsson and Berglund 2006), and can help to reduce noisy environments such as traffic noise

findings.antecedent: Biotope concept (e.g., roof gardens, restored rivers, nature parks, ponds, layered vegetation)
findings.quote: A biotope is a habitat where a specific group of plant and animal species coexist... and can be modified to work with a system approach to conserving the ecosystem and biological diversity
the medium biotope elicited the most positive emotional responses, followed by the high and then the lower biotopes.
Research has demonstrated the potential of emerging immersive display technologies to enhance soundscape evaluation, comfort, satisfaction, and overall experience in urban contexts

findings.antecedent: Immersive virtual reality experiences in green and water-dominated areas
findings.quote: immersive virtual reality experiences in green and water-dominated areas have been associated with lower stress levels

findings.antecedent: Poorly maintained green spaces (attracting undesirable activities)
findings.consequent: Negative perception of area, reduced physical activity, decreased social interaction, negative mental health impacts
findings.quote: Green spaces that are poorly maintained can attract undesirable activities such as illegal dumping, drug use, or criminal behavior. These activities create a negative perception of the area, discouraging people from utilizing the space and leading to reduced physical activity, decreased social interaction, and potential negative impacts on mental health

findings.consequent: Public health (hearing loss, cardiovascular damage, learning deficits, sleep disruption)
findings.quote: loud, annoying and sudden sounds are regarded as noise and are increasingly being identified as a public health issue with a variety of health effects, including hearing loss, cardiovascular damage, learning deficits, and sleep disruption

findings.antecedent: Low frequency sounds (e.g., wind turbines) at 30-40 dB (continued/repetitive exposure)
findings.quote: low frequency sounds (e.g. wind turbines) in the range 30-40 dB, but continued or repetitive exposure has been linked to the possibility of psychological or physiological health implications
Urban environments, on the other hand, force us to constantly engage our directed attention, which might result in mental fatigue and a lower capacity for concentration.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to green spaces or positive soundscapes
findings.consequent: Stress hormones (cortisol, adrenaline), blood pressure, heart rate
findings.quote: exposure to green spaces or positive soundscapes can reduce the production of stress hormones such as cortisol and adrenaline, lower blood pressure and heart rate, and promote relaxation and calmness

findings.antecedent: Urban settings (noise pollution, traffic congestion, social isolation)
findings.quote: Contrarily, urban settings may cause a greater physiological stress response due to factors such as noise pollution, traffic congestion, and social isolation.
Both Attention Restoration Theory and Stress Recovery Theory highlight the importance of exposure to natural environments for our cognitive and physiological well-being

findings.consequent: Comfort/satisfaction, soundscape preferences in urban environment
findings.quote: Studies have explored the soundscape and visualscape relationship perspective, with some demonstrating that visual stimuli, such as landscapes, influence the assessment of comfort/satisfaction or soundscape preferences in the urban environment
the aesthetic quality of the visual environment is the most important factor influencing soundscape perception, indicating that a more attractive visual environment improves soundscape attributes

findings.consequent: Mental health, emotional well-being (for visually impaired and non-visually impaired groups)
findings.quote: access to natural landscapes has also been shown to have positive effects on the mental health and emotional well-being of individuals with visual impairments (Shaw et al. 2015) and non-visually impaired groups (Velarde et al. 2007).

findings.consequent: Stress and mental fatigue recovery, mood, concentration, self-discipline
findings.quote: high-quality visual environments can promote stress and mental fatigue recovery, improve mood, concentration, self-discipline

findings.antecedent: Green spaces (lack of accessibility for individuals with disabilities or diverse socioeconomic backgrounds)
findings.consequent: Feelings of exclusion and inequality, decreased opportunities for physical activity, social interaction, psychophysiological health benefits
findings.quote: Lack of accessibility to greenspace for individuals with disabilities or from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds can lead to feelings of exclusion and inequality, as well as decreased opportunities for physical activity, social interaction, and the associated psychophysiological health benefits

findings.antecedent: Green spaces (close to busy roads or industrial areas, noise, air pollution, visual clutter)
findings.quote: Green spaces located close to busy roads or industrial areas may be perceived as less beneficial due to noise, air pollution, and visual clutter, which can counteract the positive effects of nature exposure on stress reduction and relaxation

findings.antecedent: Improperly designed green spaces (lack amenities, insufficient accessibility)
findings.consequent: Use for recreational activities or relaxation, inclusivity, usability
findings.quote: Improperly designed green spaces that lack amenities such as seating areas or shade may discourage people from using them for recreational activities or relaxation... Insufficient accessibility features... can limit the inclusivity and usability of green spaces

findings.consequent: Biodiversity, ecological imbalance, soil composition, nutrient cycling
findings.quote: invasive plant species can dominate green spaces, leading to a loss of biodiversity and ecological imbalance... This alteration of soil composition and nutrient cycling can have negative effects on the environment

findings.antecedent: Lack of maintenance in green spaces (overgrowth, pests, safety hazards)
findings.consequent: Health risks for nearby residents, appeal of spaces
findings.quote: the lack of maintenance in green spaces can result in overgrowth, attracting pests and posing safety hazards... This can lead to health risks for nearby residents, making the spaces unappealing

findings.antecedent: Playing soundscape (sparrow, birdsong mixture) through loudspeaker in urban public space
findings.consequent: Participants' mood, engagement, sharing, perceived traffic noise, overall soundscape quality in noise-polluted parks
findings.quote: These studies found that playing soundscape (e.g. sparrow and birdsong mixture) through a loudspeaker in an urban public space enhanced participants' mood, engagement, and sharing... as well as reduced perceived traffic noise and improved overall soundscape quality in noise-polluted parks

It has been reported that human listeners are more inclined to natural soundscapes (such as birdsong or flowing water) and generally find road traffic sounds and other by-products of the activity in cities to be unpleasant

findings.direction: more positively rated than crow sounds
findings.quote: woodpecker and sparrow sounds were rated as more positively than crow sounds in terms of perceived restorativeness of park soundscapes.
groups of bird sounds were more pleasant than those of a single species, which may be related to individuals' favourable perceptions of biodiversity.
while fox sounds were not considered pleasant, wave sounds, and bird song were rated as very pleasant.

findings.antecedent: Neurodivergent individuals (hyposensitive to soundscape, autism spectrum disorder)
findings.consequent: Difficulties in navigating urban environments, sensory overload, increased stress, challenges in focusing
findings.quote: neurodivergent individuals or those who are hyposensitive to the soundscape who encounter difficulties in navigating urban environments due to a shift in preferences and sensitivity... The constant background noise in urban areas can contribute to sensory overload, leading to increased stress and challenges in focusing and adapting to the built environment
Taller and wider tree groups were found to be the most effective in reducing noise pollution and improving soundscape quality in urban environments more than wall greening or shrubs
a small layer of 20 to 30 cm thick green wall and green facade vegetation was able to increase sound insulation for road noise by 1 dB.

findings.antecedent: Rustling of tree leaves in wind, birdsong
findings.direction: improve, feel more at ease, less stressed, less anxious
findings.quote: The rustling of tree leaves in the wind and the sound of birdsong are examples of how vegetation can be used to influence planning and design to improve mental and general health in cities... These sounds have a direct effect on people's health and help them feel more at ease, less stressed, and anxious
